title: Link congestion profiles + tensor-slicing experiments
content:
Purpose:
This note collects a set of microbenchmarks and end-to-end experiment logs investigating link congestion patterns when using tensor-slicing (model parallelism) and short-pipeline configurations. Goal: identify where throughput loss and latency spikes come from (NVLink saturation vs NIC/PCIe vs host CPU feeding), and produce a concise set of NCCL/env tuning knobs we can try in the runtime.

High-level hypothesis (prior to testing):
- Large tensor shards that require frequent all-reduce on gradients/kv-cache metadata will produce bursty NVLink traffic intra-node and stress the IB/NIC interconnect cross-node.
- Small micro-batches with pipeline stages increase the number of synchronization points and exacerbate link contention, leading to higher p99 latency even if average throughput looks OK.
- Properly sized slice/chunk + overlap of compute + transfer should reduce observed peaks and increase effective token throughput.

Hardware and software baseline:
- Nodes: 2x DGX-style nodes, each with 8x A100 80GB (NVLink mesh).
- Interconnect: Mellanox HDR200 (200Gb/s) InfiniBand between nodes.
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04 kernel 5.15 + OFED 6.x stack.
- CUDA: 12.1, NCCL: 2.18.x (build from source with MXM/UCX disabled and UCX enabled in some runs), PyTorch 2.2 nightly.
- Runtime: internal serving-runtime branch feature/parallel-shard-streaming (PR 412).
- Microbenchmark tool: nccl-tests (custom build), custom torchrun scripts to exercise tensor-slicing and pipeline stages. Profilers: nsys, nvprof for short kernels, and nvidia-smi dmon + nvlink stats via nvidia-smi nvlink -g 0

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Vary shard count (tensor-parallel groups): 1, 2, 4, 8 (intra-node hotpath).
- Vary pipeline stages: 1 (none), 2, 4.
- Batch sizes / micro-batch tokens: 1, 4, 16.
- NCCL config sets: default, NCCL_ALGO=tree, NCCL_ALGO=ring, NCCL_BUFFSIZE=1048576, NCCL_TOPO_FILE set (manual), NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS.

Representative commands used:
- nccl-tests all_reduce: "./build/all_reduce -b 8 -e 512M -f 2" (ran with mpirun across GPUs to sanity check peak allreduce throughput)
- Launch model shards: "torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 --nnodes=2 --node_rank=0 run_shard.py --tp 4 --pp 2 --micro-batch 4"
- Profiling: "nsys profile -o run_tp4_pp2 -t cuda,nvtx,osrt torchrun ..." and short kernel captures with "nvprof --profile-child-processes --print-gpu-trace ..."
- NVLink counters: "nvidia-smi nvlink -g 0" polled every 100ms via a small loop to capture transient spikes.

Key measured observations (summary):
1) Intra-node NVLink saturation is not constant: we observed short peaks (100-400ms) where a particular GPU link pair hit 80-95% of measured max, then fell back. These peaks coincide with synchronous all-reduce boundaries from tensor-sharded ops.
2) Cross-node IB utilization grows with shard count and smaller micro-batches. With tp=8 and micro-batch 1, end-to-end throughput (tokens/sec) drops ~28% compared to tp=4 for same total batch because synchronization frequency increased.
3) Switching NCCL_ALGO to tree for large power-of-two group sizes reduced p99 latency spikes by ~18% on some runs (likely fewer hops and less oscillation in buffer scheduling). However tree sometimes lost peak aggregate bandwidth versus ring for steady-state large messages.
4) Enabling NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS (force using PCIe+NVLink topology hints) helped intra-node performance when we set NCCL_BUFFSIZE to 1MB; without buffsize tuning we saw frequent re-chunking and transient stalls.
5) Pipeline stages: PP=4 with micro-batch=1 produced much higher latency variance. Increasing micro-batch to 4 reduced p99 but increased per-sample latency. There is a trade-off — for serving, micro-batch=2 or overlapping pipelined compute with async transfers appears promising.

Representative numbers (throughput and latency p50/p99):
- Config A (tp=4, pp=2, micro=4, NCCL default): 22.8k tokens/sec, p50=45ms, p99=210ms
- Config B (tp=8, pp=2, micro=1, NCCL default): 16.5k tokens/sec, p50=62ms, p99=430ms
- Config C (tp=8, pp=2, micro=1, NCCL_ALGO=tree, NCCL_BUFFSIZE=1048576): 18.9k tokens/sec, p50=55ms, p99=350ms
(These are end-to-end serving numbers from the runtime with simulated request arrival pattern, not raw nccl-tests numbers.)

Profile artifacts and what they reveal:
- nsys flamegraphs: clear vertical bands where many GPUs stall on communication syscall or NCCL ops. These align with all-reduce boundaries after an attention block.
- nvlink counter dumps: bursty TX/RX (per-link) with near-saturation windows during gradient/kv-sync points. Average link utilization was moderate, but variance large.
- nvidia-smi dmon: minimal sustained GPU SM idle during steady compute, indicating compute/comm overlap is roughly OK except around sync points.

Tuning checklist (what reduced issues in experiments):
- Increase NCCL_BUFFSIZE to ~1MB for our workloads to reduce re-chunking overheads.
- Try NCCL_ALGO=tree for group sizes >= 8 where p99 spikes dominate.
- Set NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS and provide an explicit NCCL_TOPO_FILE to encourage NVLink-first paths intra-node.
- Where cross-node traffic is high, try UCX-based transport (NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0 with UCX enabled) and set UCX_NET_DEVICES to the IB interface.
- Tune model shard sizing: avoid too many tiny shards (tp>8) when micro-batch is small. Prefer increasing micro-batch for higher tp or introduce request batching at runtime.
- Pipeline overlap: implement non-blocking send/recv + compute/transfer overlap in our streaming runtime to hide NVLink bursts. We have a prototype in PR 412.

Failure cases and oddities observed:
- On one node we saw a persistent 10-15% throughput delta versus identical node (same firmware) caused by a single GPU reporting link errors; a warm reboot and firmware reflash resolved it. Keep this in our troubleshooting checklist.
- With NCCL built without UCX we saw worse cross-node behavior for small messages; UCX + tuned NCCL_BUFFSIZE improved small-message latency significantly.

Next immediate experiments (short list):
- Run a controlled IB-only stress test (ib_send_bw with the same message sizes observed in nccl captures) to validate whether IB fabric can sustain the observed burst patterns.
- Sweep NCCL_BUFFSIZE across 128KB..4MB for tp=4 & tp=8 to find sweet spot for our attention + kv-cache patterns.
- Implement a lightweight tracepoint in runtime around shard-sync to collect exact timestamps of send/recv completion (will allow correlating NVLink bursts to model operator boundaries).
- Try 'chunked' tensor-slice strategy where we group multiple small tensors into a single larger NCCL op to reduce message count.

Decisions and proposal for runtime changes:
- Short-term: enable per-deployment default of NCCL_BUFFSIZE=1MB and explicit NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS for our NVLink clusters. Expose toggle in runtime config with rationale.
- Mid-term: implement async transfer + aggregation of small comms in the shard layer (reduce number of sync points).
- Long-term: add a topology-aware router that picks placement of shards to minimize high-contention links for hot paths (costed feature).

Notes to reviewers:
- These runs are reproducible on the lab cluster (rack-2). See linked_artifacts for PR and JIRA. The scripts used are under the PR; reach out to Priya for run ids and raw nsys captures.
- This is intentionally informal; the goal is to capture findings and next steps quickly. If we decide to standardize tuning knobs, we'll create a cleaner runbook for operations.

Unresolved questions:
- What is the safe universal NCCL_BUFFSIZE across all cluster types (PCIe-only, NVLink, mixed)?
- Can we detect at runtime when bursty syncs are about to happen and adaptively increase overlap?

End of file.
